name: Jacked & Tan 2.0
author: Cody Lefever (GZCL)
summary: A 12-week, 4-day upper/lower program in two 6-week blocks: each day works up to a rep max on a main lift, then does percentage-based volume and high-rep max-rep sets for accessories. The author says its goal is size and work capacity more than peak strength.
evidenceNote: Volume is high and nearly every accessory set is a max-rep set taken to 1-2 reps from failure, which fits current hypertrophy evidence but builds a lot of fatigue, so it suits intermediates with good recovery. Weekly rep-max work on the main lifts is not needed for muscle growth, and the write-up does not say how to set the training max, which you need for the block-1 drop sets.

sources.title: Jacked & Tan 2.0 (Swole at Every Height, Cody Lefever, 4 July 2016)

schedule: 4 sessions a week alternating lower and upper: Day 1 squat-type T1, Day 2 bench or OHP T1, Day 3 the other lower lift (deadlift or squat, different from Day 1), Day 4 the other press. An optional 5th day (an extra T1 variation, or an accessory day with no T1) is not programmed. Back work is mostly T2 and can go on either day type. Session length is not stated; 90 min is an estimate.

progression.description: Author's 2016 write-up (the 2.0 version, which replaces the 2014 original). T1: each session work up to the week's rep max (10/8/6/4/2/1RM in block 1; 6/4/2/5/3/1RM in block 2), then do drop sets. Block 1 drop sets are a percent of a training max (70, 75, 80, 82.5, 85%); block 2 drop sets are 85% then 90% of that day's RM. The last drop set is an optional rep-out. T2a: linear percent-of-TM work (50% x10x4 up to 85% x2x7), recalculated from the week-6 1RM for block 2; the write-up allows 5-10% weekly jumps early and 2.5-5% later. T2b/T2c and T3: find the week's rep max, then 3 max-rep sets with the same weight, 1-2 reps in reserve, 30-60 s rest. The write-up has two conflicting block-2 T2b/T2c lists; this template uses the detailed week-by-week section (15/12/10/6RM, then rest). Its summary table says 12/10/8/6RM. The write-up does not define how to set the TM.
progression.deload: No separate deload. Week 6 has no T2 work, week 11 drops T2b/T2c, and week 12 is only the final 1RM test. If you overshoot a rep max, cut the T1 drop sets by 2.5-5% or one set, or reduce T2 work. If the last-set rep-outs gain no extra reps for more than 3 weeks in a row, use lighter T1 drop sets. If a block-1 week 1-3 last-set rep-out exceeds 12 reps, the weight is too light and weeks 4-6 should be adjusted; if the week 7-8 rep-outs exceed +5, raise drop-set intensity moderately for the rest of block 2. If a T2a set can't be completed, lower that lift's intensity.
